title: PCT Salary Guide: What Can Patient Care Technicians Earn?
summary: Patient Care Technicians (PCTs), also known as Nurs
body_markdown:
Patient Care Technicians (PCTs), also known as[Nursing Assistants](https://www.onetonline.org/link/localtrends/31-1131.00?st=NJ&g=Go) by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, play a critical support role in the healthcare industry by performing essential tasks as directed by registered nurses or doctors.


A[PCT’s job responsibilities](https://jobs.nsh.org/career/patient-care-technician/job-descriptions#:~:text=Patient%20Care%20Technician%20Responsibilities) normally include monitoring patient vital signs, drawing blood samples, administering EKGs, and documentation of patient treatment information in medical records, among other tasks. Patient Care Technicians perform these tasks in a variety of healthcare settings, including hospitals, nursing homes, and outpatient facilities, under the direct supervision of a registered nurse or attending physician.


## How Much Do Patient Care Technicians Make?


According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, patient care technicians may also be also referred to as[nursing assistants](https://www.onetonline.org/link/localtrends/31-1131.00?st=) . The mean national average yearly salary for patient care technicians is $39,6101. However, there are many factors that affect the salaries for Patient Care Technicians, including region of the country, additional certifications earned, and the kind of facility the PCT is employed at.


### What Factors Influence PCT Salary?


#### Regional Location


The pay for a Patient Care Technician differs by employment setting (hospitals, long-term care, clinics, home health) and by location or region of the country the PCT is employed in. The top 10 metropolitan areas with the highest annual mean wage for Patient Care Technicians have[salaries that range from $47,210 to $56,530](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes311131.htm#:~:text=Top%20paying%20metropolitan%20areas) ; these metro-areas are all located in five coastal states: California, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, and Washington2. The cost of living varies widely across the United States and can affect salary levels. Keep in mind that the same 5 states that have the highest annual mean salaries are also among[the states with highest cost of living](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/banking/article/cost-of-living-by-state-map-164246259.html#:~:text=Cost%20of%20living%20by%20state:%20All) .


#### PCT Licensing, Certifications and Specialized Training


Licensing and Certifications play a role in PCT hiring, depending on your location.[California and Washington State require state-regulated licensure for Patient Care technicians](https://healthcareercerts.org/blog/patient-care-technician-requirements/#:~:text=8.%20State) . However, employers across the country prefer prospective employees to hold at least one of the 4 basic certifications3. This ensures the employer that there is a specific level of competency in the patient care technician applicant.


Patient Care Technicians usually start with one of 4 core patient care technician certifications:


1. Certified Patient Care Technician/Assistant (CPCT/A) credential from the[National Healthcareer Association](https://www.nhanow.com/certification/nha-certifications/certified-patient-care-technician-assistant-(cpct-a)) .
2. Patient Care Technician Certification (PCTC) from the[American Medical Certification Association (AMCA)](https://www.amcaexams.com/patient-care-technician-certification/) .
3. National Certified Patient Care Technician (NCPCT): Offered by the[National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT)](https://www.ncctinc.com/#:~:text=Patient%20Care%20Technician) .
4. Certified Patient Care Technician (CPCT): Offered by[American Allied Health (AAH)](https://www.americanalliedhealth.com/certification/certified-patient-care-technician-(CPCT)) .


There are also some state-specific certifications where required.


Patient Care Technicians (PCTs) can then significantly increase their skills, employability, and pay by earning specialty certifications. After earning one of the aforementioned foundational certifications, many Patient Care Technicians go on to earn additional specialized certifications, depending on their interests and opportunities.


Patient Care Technicians may pursue many specialty certifications, including4:


- Certified Clinical Hemodialysis Technician (CCHT) offered by Nephrology Nursing Certification Commission (NNCC)
- Certified Hemodialysis Technologist/Technician (CHT) offered by Board of
- Nephrology Examiners Nursing and Technology (BONENT)
- Certified Cardiographic Technician (CCT) offered by Cardiovascular Credentialing International (CCI)
- Certified EKG Technician (CET) offered by NHA, AMCA, or NCCT
- Certified Phlebotomy Technician (CPT) offered by NHA, ASCP, NCCT
- Certified Rhythm Analysis Technician (CRAT) offered by Cardiovascular Credentialing International (CCI)
- For PCTs who also hold CNA credentials can pursue Restorative Nursing Assistant (RNA)
- Basic Life Support (BLS)
- Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) offered to experienced PCTs in Emergency departments, Cardiac units, and Critical care areas.


Additional skills and capabilities make a Patient Care Technician more valuable to their employer, and this can lead to increased responsibilities that might increase salary.


#### Typical Employers of Patient Care Technicians


The industries with the highest employment levels for Patient Care Technicians are nursing care facilities, general medical and surgical hospitals, and assisted living facilities5. Experience level, employer size, union membership, and staffing demand also effect pay. Demand is a critical factor, as[healthcare occupations are projected to continue growing until at least 2035](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/) .


Shift-work can also affect salaries. Private doctor’s offices usually have one shift during the workday. Large employers, such as hospitals and nursing homes, work around the clock to care for inpatients and treat emergencies. Around-the-clock care utilizes a number of work shifts, and[night and weekend shifts generally pay more](https://experiencedalliedhealth.com/blog/shift-differential-pay-explained/) than Monday to Friday day-shift hours.


## PCT Salary Frequently Asked Questions


Lincoln Tech answers some of the most commonly ask questions regarding PCT salary:


**What is the national average mean hourly wage for patient care technicians?**
The estimated mean hourly wage for patient care technicians in the United States is $19.04 per hour1.


**Which states pay patient care technicians the most?**
Alaska, California, Oregon, Washington, and the District of Columbia6.


**How can patient care technicians increase their earning potential?**
A patient care technician can increase their earnings by gaining experience, earning specialized certifications, and/or working night and weekend shiftwork.
